| Legs | 1 |
| Page | p. 10 |

**The argument — TTW reference notes**

Swedelson argues the sport has reached a point where it is clear which programmes handle the portal best, and that no team has been better at finding and maximising quarterbacks than Miami. He traces the pattern: Cam Ward arrived having averaged 3,484 passing yards and 24 touchdowns over two Washington State seasons, then became a Heisman finalist and the No. 1 overall pick on the back of more than 4,300 yards and 39 touchdowns; Carson Beck followed from Georgia and posted a career-high 30 touchdowns. Mensah is the next in that line.

*Rests on:* quarterback (Mensah); the programme's record of portal quarterback development

**The argument — TTW reference notes**

Swedelson finds a lot to like even allowing that Kentucky is a basketball school. His central observation is that the Wildcats scored 17 points or fewer six times in 2025 and still found five wins, so a modest offensive improvement should at least hold five and clear this total. That is why they turned to Will Stein: never a head coach before, but the man who ran an Oregon offense across three seasons that made Bo Nix a first-round pick, Dillon Gabriel a third-rounder, and turned Dante Moore from a UCLA cast-off into a potential top-five pick. Kenny Minchey is the next project.

*Rests on:* coaching (Stein's quarterback development record); quarterback (Minchey); the low bar set by last year's five wins

**The argument — TTW reference notes**

Swedelson's case is Dave Doeren's consistency in year 16: he has failed to reach eight wins only once since 2020, and Swedelson says it may be neither pretty nor exciting but Doeren wins games. He acknowledges the offense that scored 30.2 points per game lost juice with Hollywood Smothers and all five leading pass catchers gone, but the reason he thinks eight wins is reachable is quarterback CJ Bailey returning for a third season and a second under coordinator Kurt Roper. He calls Bailey's decision to stay in Raleigh shocking given what the portal would have paid after 3,105 passing yards, 31 total touchdowns and nine interceptions.

*Rests on:* coaching (Doeren's floor, Roper continuity); quarterback (Bailey's return); heavy losses at receiver

He walks the slate: Utah in week two, Georgia a week later, Tulsa on September 26 as a likely win but a dreaded lookahead with Texas A&M the following week, then a brutal close from Halloween — Missouri at home, at an improved Auburn, South Carolina, at Texas, and LSU. *Rests on:* coaching (Silverfield's hire and record); schedule difficulty and sequencing; programme resources
